trial_court: Civil Judge (S.D) Mathura, Matrimonial Petition No. 144 of 2008
case_name: Smt. Payal Agrawal vs Deepak Garg
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnised in 2003 and a daughter was born in 2004. The couple filed a joint petition for dissolution of marriage under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, which was allowed and the marriage was dissolved in 2008. The husband then moved an application under Section 26 of the Hindu Marriage Act to issue directions regarding the minor child.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the marriage has broken down irretrievably.
legal_principles.held: It is held that the burden lies on the party seeking divorce to prove that the marriage has broken down irretrievably.

legal_principles.principle: The court will not grant divorce unless it is satisfied that the marriage has broken down irretrievably.
legal_principles.held: It is settled law that this court will not grant divorce unless it is satisfied that the marriage has broken down irretrievably.

outcome.final_order: The orders passed by the Additional District Judge, Mathura, dated 25.05.2009 and 14.10.2009, were quashed.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: drafting a divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
